title: The birthday that moved
summary: Model a date without inventing a midnight instant.
challenge: What date will a reader in Honolulu see if we store December 24 as midnight UTC?

title: An appointment without a place
summary: Resolve a local reading onto a timeline.
challenge: Does 09:00 identify one moment everywhere?

title: Berlin is more than +01:00
summary: Compare a region with a fixed offset.
challenge: Will the two representations still agree in summer?
code:
ZonedDateTime regional = local.atZone(ZoneId.of("Europe/Berlin"));
OffsetDateTime fixed = local.atOffset(ZoneOffset.ofHours(1));

title: It worked on my laptop
summary: Inspect the same instant in different deployment zones.
challenge: Set the simulated clock to December 23 at 23:30 UTC. Which date does each deployment see?
code:
LocalDate utcDate = instant.atZone(ZoneOffset.UTC).toLocalDate();
LocalDate berlinDate = instant.atZone(ZoneId.of("Europe/Berlin")).toLocalDate();

title: Conversion or rescheduling
summary: Choose what must survive a zone change.
challenge: Should the clock reading stay the same, or should the event happen at the same instant?
code:
ZonedDateTime display = original.withZoneSameInstant(destination);
ZonedDateTime rescheduled = original.withZoneSameLocal(destination);

title: Equal moments, different values
summary: Compare representation equality with instant equality.
challenge: Can equals be false while isEqual is true?
code:
boolean sameRepresentation = original.equals(other);
boolean sameMoment = original.isEqual(other);

title: The hour that never happened
summary: Reject a booking inside a daylight-saving gap.
challenge: What does Java do with a local reading that has zero valid offsets?

title: The hour that happened twice
summary: Resolve the two occurrences of an autumn local time.
challenge: Which 02:30 did the customer book?

title: Tomorrow is not 24 hours
summary: Separate calendar arithmetic from elapsed time.
challenge: Will adding one day and adding 24 hours produce the same local time?

title: A day without midnight
summary: Look at historical gaps at the start of a date.
challenge: What does the earliest valid time mean when a whole date was skipped?
code:
ZonedDateTime start = date.atStartOfDay(zone);
boolean dateSurvived = date.equals(start.toLocalDate());

title: The subscription that drifted
summary: Preserve an anchor for monthly recurrence.
challenge: Does January 31 plus one month twice equal January 31 plus two months?

title: A February 29 anniversary
summary: Make the non-leap-year policy explicit.
challenge: Should an anniversary fall on February 28 or March 1?

title: New Year came early
summary: Expose the week-year formatting trap.
challenge: What year will uppercase YYYY print at the edge of an ISO week year?

title: The parser fixed your date
summary: Choose strict validation at an input boundary.
challenge: Will an impossible date throw, or will the parser adjust it?

title: December or November
summary: Make numeric date order part of the contract.
challenge: Which date is 12/11/2026?
code:
LocalDate us = LocalDate.parse(input, DateTimeFormatter.ofPattern("MM/dd/uuuu", Locale.US));
LocalDate uk = LocalDate.parse(input, DateTimeFormatter.ofPattern("dd/MM/uuuu", Locale.UK));

challenge: Does a Java timestamp survive the database column and JDBC driver unchanged?

challenge: How many elapsed hours belong to this business date?

title: Three working days later

challenge: What happens when the countdown crosses Christmas?

title: The rules changed

challenge: Should a future promise preserve 09:00 local or its previously calculated instant?

challenge: Is the exact unlock instant included?

title: The midnight job
summary: Recover a due job and commit one local database effect.
challenge: What survives a rollback, a late worker, and a repeated delivery attempt?
code:
INSERT INTO gift_effect (job_id, delivered_at, message)
SELECT id, ?, 'A small gift from the calendar'
FROM scheduled_gift
WHERE id = ? AND due_at <= ?
ON CONFLICT (job_id) DO NOTHING;
-- Commit the local effect, or roll back the complete transaction.
